The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said to a boy: O boy, say Bismillaah, eat with your right hand, and eat from what is in front of you.
The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Spread salam between you.
A man asked the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, what is best in Islam. He said: Feed people, and say salam to those you know and those you do not know.
The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: If it were not too hard for my people, or he said: for people, I would tell them to use the miswak with every prayer.
Aishah said: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, liked to start with the right: putting on his shoes, combing his hair, making wudu, and in everything he did.
The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: When you go to bed, make wudu as you do for the prayer, then lie down on your right side.
Anas said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, used to take three breaths while drinking.
Anas said about the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him,: He told people not to drink standing up.
Aishah was asked what the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, did at home. She said: He used to help his family with their work. When it was time to pray, he went out to the prayer.
The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Feed the hungry, visit the sick, and set the prisoner free.

The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, told of a man who gave water to a thirsty dog, and Allah forgave him. The Companions asked if there is a reward for kindness to animals. He said: There is a reward for kindness to every living thing.
The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said that faith has many branches: and the smallest of them is moving something harmful out of the road.
The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should say something good or stay quiet.
The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Jibril kept telling me to be good to the neighbour, until I thought he would make the neighbour inherit.
A man asked the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, for advice, again and again. Each time he said: Do not get angry.
The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Make things easy and do not make them hard. Give good news and do not drive people away.
The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself.
Abu Hurayrah said: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, never found fault with any food. If he liked it, he ate it, and if not, he left it.
The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Allah is pleased with a servant who eats some food and praises Him for it, or drinks a drink and praises Him for it.
The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: When one of you goes into the masjid, he should pray two rak'ahs before he sits down.
The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was asked about fasting on Monday. He said: That is the day I was born.

The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: The du-aa of a Muslim for his brother when he is not there is answered. An angel is beside him. Each time he asks for good for his brother, the angel says: Ameen, and the same for you.
The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: When one of you yawns, he should put his hand over his mouth.
The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, named five things from the fitrah, the natural way. One of them is: cutting the nails.
The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Gentleness is never in anything without making it beautiful, and it is never taken out of anything without spoiling it.
The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Truthfulness leads to goodness, and goodness leads to Jannah.
The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: A good word is a charity.
The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Whoever says Subhaan Allahi wa bihamdihi a hundred times in a day, his sins are wiped away, even if they were like the foam of the sea.
The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Whoever walks a path looking for knowledge, Allah makes easy for him a path to Jannah.
Abu Barzah said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, did not like sleeping before Isha, or talking after it.
The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Food for one is enough for two, and food for two is enough for four.

A man came to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and asked: O Messenger of Allah, who most deserves my good company? He said: Your mother. The man asked: Then who? He said: Your mother. He asked: Then who? He said: Your mother. He asked: Then who? He said: Then your father.
The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Purity is half of faith.
He, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Whoever is not merciful will not be shown mercy.

Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, kissed his grandson al-Hasan while al-Aqra' was sitting with him. Al-Aqra' said: I have ten children and I have never kissed any of them. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, looked at him and said: Whoever is not merciful will not be shown mercy.

He, peace and blessings be upon him, called the people of Makkah together at the hill of as-Safa and asked: If I told you that horsemen in the valley were about to attack you, would you believe me? They said: Yes. We have only ever known you to tell the truth.
Jabir said: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was never asked for anything and said no.

Anas said: I had a little brother called Abu Umayr. I think he had just been weaned. Whenever the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, came, he would say: O Abu Umayr, what did the little bird do? It was a little bird that he played with.
Anas said: I served the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, for ten years. He never said to me Uff, and never said: Why did you do that? or: Why didn't you do that?
Jarir said: Since I became Muslim, the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, never kept me away, and he never saw me without smiling at me.
He, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Real patience is at the first moment of the hurt.

He, peace and blessings be upon him, prayed at night until his feet were swollen. Aishah said: Why do you do this, O Messenger of Allah, when Allah has forgiven you everything? He said: Should I not love to be a thankful servant?
One night the people of Madinah heard a frightening noise. He, peace and blessings be upon him, had already ridden out to check, and he came back saying: Do not be afraid, do not be afraid.
A man gave a gift to one of his sons only. He, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Fear Allah, and be fair between your children.

He, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Allah did not send any Prophet who did not look after sheep. His Companions asked: And you? He said: Yes. I looked after them for the people of Makkah, for a few coins.
Aishah said: He used to go alone to the cave of Hira and worship Allah there.
The people of Makkah said to him: We have only ever known you to tell the truth.
Abu Bakr was afraid they would be seen. He, peace and blessings be upon him, said: O Abu Bakr, what do you think of two people when Allah is the third with them?
Anas said: They carried the stones, chanting as they worked, and the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was with them.

Abdullah ibn Mas'ud said: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, entered Makkah on the day of the conquest. There were three hundred and sixty idols around the Ka'bah. He struck them with a stick in his hand, saying: The truth has come and falsehood has gone.
Aishah said: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, passed away when he was sixty-three.
The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: The best day the sun rises on is Friday.
The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: The best fasting after Ramadan is in Allah's month, Muharram.
The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Fasting the day of Ashura: I hope Allah will forgive for it the year before.
The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Look for Laylat al-Qadr in the odd nights of the last ten nights of Ramadan.
The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: No good deeds on other days are better than good deeds on these ten days.
The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Fasting the Day of Arafah: I hope Allah will forgive for it the year before and the year after.

Narrated Ibn Masud: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, used to take care of us in preaching by selecting a suitable time, so that we might not get bored. He abstained from pestering us with sermons and knowledge all the time,
Narrated Ibn Abbas: Once the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, embraced me and said, O Allah! Bestow on him the knowledge of the Book, Quran,
Narrated Uthman: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, The best among you, Muslims, are those who learn the Quran and teach it

Narrated Ibn Umar: Allah's Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, said, The example of the person who knows the Quran by heart is like the owner of tied camels. If he keeps them tied, he will control them, but if he releases them, they will run away

Narrated Abu Moosaa: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, Commit yourself to the Quran, for by Him in whose Hand is my soul, it is surely more prone to break away than a camel in its bind

Narrated Aisha: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, heard a man reciting the Quran in the mosque and said, May Allah bestow His Mercy on him, as he has reminded me of such-and-such Verses of such a Surah

Narrated Abdullah: That the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said to him, Recite the Quran to me. Abdullah said, Shall I recite, the Quran, to you while it has been revealed to you? He said, I like to hear it from others

Narrated Abdullah bin Amr: Allah's Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, said to me, Recite the whole Quran in one month's time. I said, But I have power, to do more than that. Allah's Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, said, Then finish the recitation of the Quran in seven days, and do not finish it in less than this period

Narrated An-Numan bin Bashir: Allah's Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, said, You see the believers as regards their being merciful among themselves and showing love among themselves and being kind, resembling one body, so that, if any part of the body is not well then the whole body shares the sleeplessness, insomnia, and fever with it

Narrated Anas bin Malik: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, If any Muslim plants any plant and a human being or an animal eats of it, he will be rewarded as if he had given that much in charity

Narrated Anas bin Malik: Allah's Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, said, Do not hate one another, and do not be jealous of one another, and do not desert each other, and O, Allah's worshipers! Be brothers. Lo! It is not permissible for any Muslim to desert, not talk to, his brother, Muslim, for more than three days

Narrated Abu Huraira: Allah's Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, said, The strong is not the one who overcomes the people by his strength, but the strong is the one who controls himself while in anger

Narrated Anas bin Malik: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, Make things easy for the people, and do not make it difficult for them, and make them calm, with glad tidings, and do not repulse, them,

Narrated Abu Huraira: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, should not hurt his neighbor and whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, should serve his guest generously and whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, should speak what is good or keep silent
Narrated Abdullah: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, Everyone will be with those whom he loves

Narrated Anas bin Malik: Two men sneezed before the Prophet. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said to one of them, May Allah bestow His Mercy on you, but he did not say that to the other. On being asked, why, the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, That one praised Allah, at the time of sneezing, while the other did not praise Allah

Narrated Abu Huraira: Allah's Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, said, The younger person should greet the older one, and the walking person should greet the sitting one, and the small number of persons should greet the large number of persons
Narrated 'Abdullah bin 'Amr: A man asked the Prophet, What Islamic traits are the best? The Prophet said, Feed the people, and greet those whom you know and those whom you do not know

Narrated Abu Aiyub: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, It is not lawful for a Muslim to desert, not to speak to, his brother Muslim for more than three days while meeting, one turns his face to one side and the other turns his face to the other side. Lo! The better of the two is the one who starts greeting the other
Narrated Anas: Whenever Allah's Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, greeted somebody, he used to greet him three times, and if he spoke a sentence, he used to repeat it thrice

Narrated Aisha: Allah's Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, said, Do good deeds properly, sincerely and moderately and know that your deeds will not make you enter Paradise, and that the most beloved deed to Allah is the most regular and constant even if it were little

Narrated Abdullah bin Amr: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, A Muslim is the one who avoids harming Muslims with his tongue or his hands. And a Muhajir, an emigrant, is the one who gives up, abandons, all what Allah has forbidden

Abu Huraira reported that a person came to Allah, 's Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, and said: Who among the people is most deserving of a fine treatment from my hand? He said: Your mother. He again said: Then who, is the next one? He said: Again it is your mother, who deserves the best treatment from you. He said: Then who, is the next one? He, the Holy Prophet, said: Again, it is your mother. He, again, said: Then who? Thereupon he said: Then it is your father. In the hadith transmitted on the authority of Qutalba, there is no mention of the word the people

Ibn Dinar reported that a desert Arab met Abdullah b. 'Umar on the way to Mecca. 'Abdullah greeted him and mounted him upon the donkey on which he had been riding and gave him the turban that he had on his head. Ibn Dinar, further, reported: We said to him, 'Abdullah b. 'Umar,: May Allah do good to you, these are desert Arabs and they are satisfied even with meagre, things. Thereupon Abdullah said: His father was loved dearly by 'Umar b. Khattib and I heard Allah's Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, as saying: The finest act of goodness on the part of a son is to treat kindly the loved ones of his father

Nawwas b. Sam'an al-Ansari reported: I asked Allah's Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, about virtue and vice. He said: Virtue is a kind disposition and vice is what rankles in your heart and that you disapprove that people should come to know of it

Abu Huraira reported Allah's Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, as saying: Charity does not decrease wealth, no one forgives another except that Allah increases his honor, and no one humbles himself for the sake of Allah except that Allah raises his status
Abu Barza reported: I said: Allah's Messenger, teach me something so that I may derive benefit from it. He said: Remove the troublesome thing from the paths of the Muslims

A'isha reported Allah's Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, as saying: Gabriel impressed upon me, kind treatment, towards the neighbour, so much, that I thought as if he would confer upon him the, right, of inheritance

Abu Dharr reported: Allah's Apostle, peace and blessings be upon him, said to me: Don't consider anything insignificant out of good things even if it is that you meet your brother with a cheerful countenance

Abu Huraira reported Allah's Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, as saying: Two are the expressions which are light on the tongue, but heavy in scale, dear to the Compassionate One: Hallowed be Allah and praise is due to Him ; Hallowed be Allah, the Great

Khaula bint Hakim Sulamiyya reported: I heard Allah's Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, as saying: When anyone lands at a place, and then says: I seek refuge in the Perfect Word of Allah from the evil of what He has created, nothing would harm him until he marches from that stopping place
The believers are brothers and sisters.
If you tried to count Allah’s blessings, you could never count them all.
Do good. Allah loves those who do good.
Those who hold back their anger and forgive people.
Allah tells you to give back the things you are trusted with to their owners.
Whoever puts their trust in Allah, He is enough for them.
So race each other to do good.
Eat of its fruit when it gives fruit.
Do not spread harm on the earth after it has been set right.
Keep your promises. You will be asked about your promises.
Glory be to the One who has made this work for us, when we could never have done it ourselves.
We made you into nations and tribes so that you may get to know one another.
Allah is the Creator of everything.
Say: He is Allah, the One.
Allah is the One who provides.
When My servants ask about Me, I am near.
Every good thing you have is from Allah.
He sees everything.
Our Lord, You did not create this for nothing. Glory be to You.
You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help.
Allah has the most beautiful Names, so call on Him by them.
We said: O fire, be cool and safe for Ibrahim.
Your God is One God. There is no god but Him, the Most Merciful, the Most Kind.
Nuh said: Ride in it. In the name of Allah it sails and it stops. My Lord is Forgiving and Merciful.
There is no god but You. Glory be to You. I have been one of those who did wrong.
Moosaa said: No! My Lord is with me. He will guide me.
The renewed digging of Zamzam by Abd al-Muttalib ibn Hashim. Its traces had been worn away after the tribe of Jurhum filled it in, and so it remained until his time.

When its matter had been made clear to him and its place had been shown to him, and he knew he had been told the truth, he set out in the morning with his pickaxe, and with him his son al-Harith ibn Abd al-Muttalib, who was his only son at that time. He dug, and when the stone lining of the old well appeared, Abd al-Muttalib called out Allaahu Akbar, and Quraysh knew that he had found what he was looking for.

They came to him and said: Abd al-Muttalib, this is the well of our father Ismail, and we have a right to it. Give us a share in it with you. He said: I will not. This matter was given to me alone, out of all of you. They said: Then be fair to us, for we will not leave you until we have taken you to judgement over it.

Then Abd al-Muttalib set up the watering of the pilgrims from Zamzam. Ibn Ishaq and others mention that there were many wells in Makkah before Zamzam appeared in the time of Abd al-Muttalib … and Zamzam surpassed all the wells, and all the people turned to it, because of its place by the Sacred Mosque, its excellence over all other water, and because it is the well of Ismail son of Ibrahim.

What Allah did to the People of the Elephant was not a victory for Quraysh … rather, the victory was for the Sacred House, as a sign and a preparation for the sending of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him.
I say: in its year the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was born, according to the well-known view.

He was born, blessings and peace be upon him, on a Monday, because of what Muslim narrated in his Sahih, from the hadith of Ghaylan ibn Jarir from Abdullah ibn Mabad al-Zimmani from Abu Qatada: a Bedouin said, O Messenger of Allah, what do you say about fasting on Monday? He said: That is the day on which I was born, and on which revelation was sent down to me.
Then the majority hold that it was in the month of Rabi al-Awwal.

Ibn Ishaq said: His birth, blessings and peace be upon him, was in the Year of the Elephant, and this is what is well known from the majority. Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir al-Hizami said: It is something none of our scholars doubts, that he, blessings and peace be upon him, was born in the Year of the Elephant, and was sent as a prophet at the head of forty years from the Elephant.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: al-Muttalib ibn Abdullah ibn Qays ibn Makhrama told me, from his father, from his grandfather Qays ibn Makhrama, who said: I and the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, were born in the Year of the Elephant. We were the same age.
Khalifa ibn Khayyat said: What is agreed upon is that he, peace be upon him, was born in the Year of the Elephant.
Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: A nurse was found for him, blessings and peace be upon him: Halima bint Abi Dhuayb.
And his brother and sisters, blessings and peace be upon him, by nursing: Abdullah ibn al-Harith, Unaysa bint al-Harith, and Hudhafa bint al-Harith, who is al-Shayma.

So the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was with his mother Amina bint Wahb and his grandfather Abd al-Muttalib, in Allah’s care and keeping. Allah made him grow up well, for the honour He intended for him.

When Abd al-Muttalib ibn Hashim died, the watering of the pilgrims and Zamzam passed after him to his son al-Abbas, one of the youngest of his brothers. It stayed with him until Islam came, and the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, left it in his hands.

After his grandfather Abd al-Muttalib, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was with his uncle Abu Talib, because Abd al-Muttalib had entrusted him to him, and because Abu Talib was the full brother of his father Abdullah: their mother was Fatima bint Amr ibn Aidh ibn Imran ibn Makhzum. Abu Talib was the one who took charge of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, after his grandfather; he was in his care and with him.

The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Allah did not send any prophet except that he was a shepherd. His companions said to him: And you, O Messenger of Allah? He said: And I tended them for the people of Makkah for a few qirats.

Its cause was that a man from Zubayd came to Makkah with goods. Al-As ibn Wail bought them from him and then held back what he owed him. The man from Zubayd asked the allied clans, Abd al-Dar, Makhzum, Jumah, Sahm and Adi ibn Kab, to help him against him, and they refused to help against al-As ibn Wail.
When the man from Zubayd saw how badly he was treated, he climbed up on Abu Qubays at sunrise, while Quraysh were sitting in their gatherings around the Kabah, and called out at the top of his voice.

The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: I witnessed, in the house of Abdullah ibn Judan, an alliance which, if I were called to it in Islam, I would answer. They allied to return what is owed to its rightful people, and that no wrongdoer would overpower someone wronged.
When he came back to Makkah to Khadija with her goods, she sold what he had brought, and it came to double, or nearly.
Ibn Ishaq said: al-Fijar was twenty years after the Elephant. The building of the Kabah was fifteen years after al-Fijar, and his being sent as a prophet was five years after its building.
When the Kabah was built, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, went to carry stones.

When the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was thirty-five years old, Quraysh gathered to build the Kabah. They had been wanting to do it, to give it a roof, but they were afraid to take it down. It was only loose stones laid without mortar, a little higher than a man, and they wanted to raise it and roof it.
The sea had thrown up a ship at Jeddah, belonging to a merchant of the Romans, and it was broken up. They took its timber and made it ready for the roof.
There was in Makkah a Coptic man who was a carpenter, and he got ready for them some of what was needed.
He said: People of Quraysh, put nothing of your earnings into its building except what is good and lawful.

Then Quraysh divided the Kabah between them. The side of the door was for Banu Abd Manaf and Zuhra. Between the Black Corner and the Yemeni Corner was for Banu Makhzum and the clans of Quraysh who joined them. The back of the Kabah was for Banu Jumah and Sahm. The side of al-Hijr was for Banu Abd al-Dar ibn Qusayy, Banu Asad ibn Abd al-Uzza and Banu Adi ibn Kab: that is al-Hatim.
Quraysh stayed like that for four or five nights. Then they gathered in the Mosque, consulted one another and agreed to be fair.
Hira, is a mountain in upper Makkah, three miles from it, on the left of whoever goes to Mina. It has a peak that leans over, facing the Kabah, and the cave is in that bend.

The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, used to stay at Hira for one month every year, in devotion. That was something Quraysh held dear in the time before Islam. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would stay that month every year, feeding the poor who came to him. When he had finished his month, the first thing he did when he left, before going into his house, was go to the Kabah and go round it seven times, or as many as Allah willed. Then he would go back to his house.

Aisha said: The first of the revelation that came to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was true dreams in his sleep. He did not see a dream but it came true like the breaking of dawn.

Then being alone was made dear to him. He would go alone to the cave of Hira and worship there for a number of nights, before going back to his family, and he would take provisions for that. Then he would go back to Khadija and take provisions for the same again, until the truth came to him while he was in the cave of Hira.
The correct view is that his words I am not one who reads are a denial: that is, I am not someone who knows how to read.

The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, went back with them, his heart trembling, and went in to Khadija bint Khuwaylid. He said: Cover me, cover me. They covered him until the fear left him. He told Khadija what had happened and said to her: I feared for myself.

Khadija said: No, by Allah, Allah will never disgrace you. You keep the ties of kinship, you honour the guest, you carry the burden of the weak, you give to those who have nothing, and you help in the hardships that come by right.
So said Ubayd ibn Umayr, Abu Jafar al-Baqir and more than one of the scholars: that revelation came to him on a Monday. There is no disagreement among them about this.
The well-known view is that he was sent as a prophet in the month of Ramadan, as Ubayd ibn Umayr, Muhammad ibn Ishaq and others stated.
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, began to speak of all that Allah had blessed him and His servants with, of prophethood, in secret, to those of his family he trusted.
Ibn Ishaq said: Khadija was the first to believe in Allah and His Messenger, and to accept as true what he brought.
Ibn Haritha, meaning Zayd, accepted Islam too. The two of them stayed like that for nearly a month, with Ali coming and going to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him.

The first of the free men to accept Islam was Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, and his Islam brought more benefit than that of those mentioned before, because he was a man of high standing, an honoured chief in Quraysh, a man of wealth, and one who called others to Islam. He was loved and brought people together, and spent his wealth in obedience to Allah and His Messenger.
Abu Bakr, was a merchant of good character and kindness. The men of his people would come to him and enjoy his company for more than one reason: his knowledge, his trade and his good company.

They went to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, with Abu Bakr. He offered them Islam, recited the Quran to them and told them the truth of Islam, and they believed. These were the eight who came before, the people, to Islam. They believed the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and believed in what came from Allah.
Then people entered, Islam, in group after group, men and women, until the news of Islam spread in Makkah and people talked about it.
When the Companions of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, prayed, they would go out into the mountain passes and hide their prayer from their people.

Ibn Ishaq said: Then, three years after he was sent, Allah commanded His Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, to proclaim openly what he had been commanded, and to be patient with the harm of the idol-worshippers.

Al-Waqidi narrated that they set out for it in Rajab, in the fifth year after the sending, and that the first of them to emigrate were eleven men and four women. They reached the sea, some walking and some riding, and hired a ship to Abyssinia for half a dinar.
Umm Salama said: So we went out to it in groups until we had all gathered there. We settled in the best of homes, next to the best of neighbours, safe in our religion, and we feared no wrong there.

When Quraysh saw that we had found a home and safety, they were jealous of us. They agreed to send to the Negus about us, to have us driven out of his land and sent back to them. They sent Amr ibn al-As and Abdullah ibn Abi Rabia, and gathered gifts for him and for his generals, and did not leave out a single general without preparing a gift for him.
One of the gifts from Makkah he liked best was leather.

He became angry and said: No, by the life of Allah! I will not hand them back until I have called them, spoken to them and seen what their matter is. They are people who sought refuge in my land and chose my protection over anyone else’s. If they are as these men say, I will hand them back. If they are otherwise, I will protect them and not come between them and their people, and I will not please these two.

He said: Come, recite to me some of what he brought. So he recited to him the beginning of Kaf Ha Ya Ayn Sad, Surah Maryam. By Allah, the Negus wept until his beard was wet, and his bishops wept until their scrolls were wet, when they heard what he recited to them. Then he said, to them,: This speech comes from the same lamp-niche that Moosaa brought. Go, rightly guided. No, by Allah, I will not hand them over to you, and I will not please you.

Banu Hashim stayed in their valley for three years, and the hardship and strain on them grew severe. Quraysh cut them off from the markets: of the food that came to Makkah and the goods for sale, they let none reach them, but hurried to it first and bought it.

At the end of three years, men of Banu Abd Manaf, of Qusayy, and others of Quraysh whose mothers were from Banu Hashim, began to blame one another. They saw that they had cut the ties of kinship and made light of what was right. That same night they agreed to break the treacherous pact they had made, and to free themselves of it.
And Allah sent the termite against their document, and it ate away every pledge and promise in it.

Ibn Abbas said: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was sent at the age of forty. He stayed thirteen years, in Makkah, receiving revelation, then he was commanded to emigrate, and he lived as an emigrant for ten years. He died at the age of sixty-three.
His Hijrah, peace be upon him, was in the month of Rabi al-Awwal, in the thirteenth year after he was sent, and it was on a Monday.

When Abu Bakr had asked the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, for permission to emigrate, he had said to him: Do not hurry. Perhaps Allah will give you a companion. Abu Bakr hoped that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, meant himself, so he bought two riding camels and kept them at his house, feeding them to be ready for it.
Al-Waqidi said: he bought them for eight hundred dirhams.

Then he said: O Prophet of Allah, these are two camels I had made ready for this. They hired Abdullah ibn Arqat, Ibn Hisham says he is also called Abdullah ibn Urayqit, a man of Banu al-Duil ibn Bakr whose mother was from Banu Sahm ibn Amr. He was an idol-worshipper, and he was to show them the road. They handed their two camels to him, and he kept them, grazing them, until the time they had agreed.

As for Ali, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, told him to stay behind and give back, on behalf of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, the things people had left in his keeping. There was no one in Makkah who had something he feared for but left it with him, because they knew his truthfulness and his trustworthiness.

When the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, had made up his mind, to leave, he came to Abu Bakr ibn Abi Quhafa, and the two of them went out through a small door at the back of Abu Bakr’s house.
Asma bint Abi Bakr, may Allah be pleased with her, would bring them food in the evening, what they needed.

Abu Bakr, said: I said to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, while we were in the cave: If one of them looked down at his feet, he would see us beneath his feet. He said: O Abu Bakr, what do you think of two, when Allah is their third?

The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, met al-Zubayr with a party of Muslims, merchants on their way back from al-Sham, to Makkah, and al-Zubayr gave the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and Abu Bakr white clothes to wear.

Abu Bakr stood to greet the people, and the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, sat in silence. Those of the Ansar who came and had never seen the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, began greeting Abu Bakr, until the sun reached the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and Abu Bakr came and shaded him with his cloak. Then the people knew which one was the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him.

The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, stayed among Banu Amr ibn Awf for some ten-odd nights. He founded the mosque that was founded on taqwa, and the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, prayed in it.

The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, began carrying the mud bricks with them as they built it, saying as he carried them: This load is not the load of Khaybar: this, our Lord, is more righteous and purer. And he said: O Allah, the reward is the reward of the Hereafter, so have mercy on the Ansar and the Muhajirun.
Ibn Umar said, that in the time of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, the mosque was built of mud bricks, its roof was of palm branches, and its pillars were palm trunks.
Anas said: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, made a pact of brotherhood between the Muhajirun and the Ansar in our house.

Abu Bakr and Kharija ibn Zayd al-Khazraji were brothers; Umar ibn al-Khattab and Itban ibn Malik were brothers; Abu Ubayda and Sad ibn Muadh were brothers; and Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf and Sad ibn al-Rabi were brothers.

Anas said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf came, to Madinah, and the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, made him a brother of Sad ibn al-Rabi al-Ansari. Sad offered to share his household and his wealth with him, half and half. Abd al-Rahman said: May Allah bless you in your household and your wealth. Show me the market. And he made a profit of some dried curd and butter.

He, peace and blessings be upon him, said: It is a true dream, if Allah wills. Stand with Bilal and teach it to him, and let him call it, for his voice is more beautiful than yours. When Bilal called it, Umar ibn al-Khattab heard it in his house and came out to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, dragging his cloak, saying: O Prophet of Allah, by the One who sent you with the truth, I saw the same as he saw. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: To Allah be the praise, for that.
Uhud was named Uhud because it stands alone among those mountains. In the Sahih: Uhud is a mountain that loves us, and we love it.
It was in Dhu al-Qada of the year six, without disagreement.

The Companions of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, had set out with no doubt that they would enter Makkah, because of a dream the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, had seen. When they saw the peace and the turning back, and what the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, had taken on himself, it weighed on the people so heavily that they were almost overcome.
He, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Tonight a surah has been sent down to me that is dearer to me than everything the sun rises on.

When the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, had settled in Makkah and the people were calm, he went out to the House and went round it seven times on his camel, touching the Corner with a crooked stick in his hand. When he had finished going round, he called Uthman ibn Talha and took the key of the Kabah from him. It was opened for him, and he went in.

A man of the Jews said to Umar: Commander of the Believers, you recite a verse in your Book which, if it had come down to us Jews, we would have taken that day as a festival. He said: Which verse? He said: This day I have perfected your religion for you, completed My favour upon you, and chosen Islam as your religion. Umar said: By Allah, I know the day it was sent down to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and the hour it was sent down: the evening of Arafa, on a Friday.

I have left among you something after which you will not go astray if you hold fast to it: the Book of Allah. And you will be asked about me, so what will you say? They said: We bear witness that you have conveyed the message, given sincere counsel and done your duty. He raised his forefinger to the sky and pointed it at the people: O Allah, bear witness. O Allah, bear witness, three times.

On the authority of Abdullah, the son of Umar ibn al-Khattab, ra, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, say, Islam has been built on five, pillars,: testifying that there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, establishing the salah, prayer, paying the zakaah, obligatory charity, making the hajj, pilgrimage, to the House, and fasting in Ramadhan. Bukhari & Muslim,

On the authority of an-Nu’man ibn Basheer, ra, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, say, That which is lawful is clear and that which is unlawful is clear, and between the two of them are doubtful matters about which many people do not know. Thus he who avoids doubtful matters clears himself in regard to his religion and his honor, but he who falls into doubtful matters, eventually, falls into that which is unlawful, like the shepherd who pastures around a sanctuary, all but grazing therein. Truly every king has a sanctuary, and truly Allah’s sanctuary is His prohibitions. Truly in the body there is a morsel of flesh, which, if it be whole, all the body is whole, and which, if it is diseased, all of, the body, is diseased. Truly, it is the heart. Bukhari & Muslim,

On the authority of Tameem ibn Aus ad-Daree, ra,: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, The deen, religion, is naseehah, advice, sincerity. We said, To whom? He, peace and blessings be upon him, said, To Allah, His Book, His Messenger, and to the leaders of the Muslims and their common folk. Muslim,

On the authority of Abu Hurayrah, ra,: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, Allah the Almighty is Good and accepts only that which is good. And verily Allah has commanded the believers to do that which He has commanded the Messengers. So the Almighty has said: O, you, Messengers! Eat of the tayyibat [all kinds of halal, legal, foods], and perform righteous deeds. 23: 51, and the Almighty has said: O you who believe! Eat of the lawful things that We have provided you. 2: 172, Then he, peace and blessings be upon him, mentioned, the case, of a man who, having journeyed far, is disheveled and dusty, and who spreads out his hands to the sky saying O Lord! O Lord! while his food is haram, unlawful, his drink is haram, his clothing is haram, and he has been nourished with haram, so how can, his supplication, be answered? Muslim,

On the authority of Abu Hamzah Anas bin Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, the servant of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, that the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: None of you, truly, believes until he loves for his brother that which he loves for himself. Al-Bukhari, Muslim,

On the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: Let him who believes in Allah and the Last Day speak good, or keep silent; and let him who believes in Allah and the Last Day be generous to his neighbour; and let him who believes in Allah and the Last Day be generous to his guest. Al-Bukhari, Muslim,

On the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him,: A man said to the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, Counsel me, so he, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, Do not become angry. The man repeated, his request for counsel, several times, and, each time, he, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, Do not become angry. Al-Bukhari,

On the authority of Abu Masood Uqbah bin ’Amr al-Ansaree al-Badree, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, Verily, from what was learnt by the people from the speech of the earliest prophecy is: If you feel no shame, then do as you wish. Al-Bukhari,

On the authority of Abu Amr, and he is also called Abu Amrah, Sufyan bin Abdullah ath- Thaqafee, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I said, O Messenger of Allah, tell me something about al-Islam which I can ask of no one but you. He, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, Say I believe in Allah, and then be steadfast. Muslim,

On the authority of Abu Abdullah Jabir bin Abdullah al-Ansaree, may Allah be pleased with him, that: A man questioned the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and said, Do you think that if I perform the obligatory prayers, fast in Ramadhan, treat as lawful that which is halal, and treat as forbidden that which is haram, and do not increase upon that, in voluntary good deeds, then I shall enter Paradise? He, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, replied, Yes. Muslim,

On the authority of Abu Malik al-Harith bin Asim al-Asharee, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, Purity is half of iman, faith. Al-hamdu lillah, praise be to Allah, fills the scales, and subhan-Allah, how far is Allah from every imperfection, and Al-hamdulillah, praise be to Allah, fill that which is between heaven and earth. And the salah, prayer, is a light, and charity is a proof, and patience is illumination, and the Quran is a proof either for you or against you. Every person starts his day as a vendor of his soul, either freeing it or causing its ruin. Muslim,

On the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, Every joint of a person must perform a charity each day that the sun rises: to judge justly between two people is a charity. To help a man with his mount, lifting him onto it or hoisting up his belongings onto it, is a charity. And the good word is a charity. And every step that you take towards the prayer is a charity, and removing a harmful object from the road is a charity. Al-Bukhari, Muslim,

On the authority of Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, from what he has related from his Lord: Verily Allah ta’ala has written down the good deeds and the evil deeds, and then explained it, by saying,: Whosoever intended to perform a good deed, but did not do it, then Allah writes it down with Himself as a complete good deed. And if he intended to perform it and then did perform it, then Allah writes it down with Himself as from ten good deeds up to seven hundred times, up to many times multiplied. And if he intended to perform an evil deed, but did not do it, then Allah writes it down with Himself as a complete good deed. And if he intended it, i.e. the evil deed, and then performed it, then Allah writes it down as one evil deed. Al-Bukhari, Muslim,

Narrated Said bin Jubair: Those Suras which you people call the Mufassal, are the Muhkam. And Ibn Abbas said, Allah's Apostle died when I was a boy of ten years, and I had learnt the Muhkam, of the Quran,

Narrated Masriq: Abdullah bin Amr mentioned Abdullah bin Masud and said, I shall ever love that man, for I heard the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, saying, 'Take, learn, the Quran from four: Abdullah bin Masud, Salim, Muadh and Ubai bin Kab

It was narrated that Umm Hisham bin Harithah bin An-Nu'man said: Our oven and the oven of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, were the same for two years, or for one year and part of a year. And I only learned Surah Qaf. By the Glorious Quran from the tongue of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, who used to recited it every Friday from the Minbar, when he addresses the people

Narrated Abdullah: Allah's Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, said, Do not wish to be like anyone, except in two cases: A man whom Allah has given wealth and he spends it righteously. A man whom Allah has given wisdom, knowledge of the Quran and the Hadith, and he acts according to it and teaches it to others

Narrated Abdullah bin Umar: Allah's Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, said, Not to wish to be the like except of two men. A man whom Allah has given the knowledge of the Book and he recites it during the hours of the night, and a man whom Allah has given wealth, and he spends it in charity during the night and the hours of the day

Anas reported Allah's Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, as saying to Ubayy b. Ka'b: Allah has commanded me to recite the Quran to you. He said: Did Allah mention me to you by name? He, the Holy Prophet, said: Allah made a mention of your name to me. On hearing this, Ubayy b. Ka'b wept

Narrated Abu Said Al-Khudri: A man heard another man reciting, Surat-Al-Ikhlas, 'Say He is Allah, the, One.' repeatedly. The next morning he came to Allah's Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, and informed him about it as if he thought that it was not enough to recite. On that Allah's Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, said, By Him in Whose Hand my life is, this Surah is equal to one-third of the Quran

Narrated 'Aisha: Whenever the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, went to bed every night, he used to cup his hands together and blow over it after reciting Surat Al-Ikhlas, Surat Al-Falaq and Surat An-Nas, and then rub his hands over whatever parts of his body he was able to rub, starting with his head, face and front of his body. He used to do that three times

Jundub b. 'Abdullah al-Bajali reported Allah's Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, as saying: Recite the Quran as long as your hearts agree to do so, and when you feel variance between them, between your hearts and tongues, then get up, and leave its recital for the time being,

Narrated Abu Huraira: Allah's Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, said, Allah does not listen to a prophet as He listens to a prophet who recites the Quran in a pleasant tone. The companion of the sub-narrator, Abu Salama, said, It means, reciting it aloud
Narrated Abu Moosaa: That the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said to him' O Abu Moosaa! You have been given one of the mazamir, sweet melodious voices, of the family of David

Abu Burda narrated on the authority of Abu Moosaa that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, had said to Abu Moosaa: If you were to see me, as I was listening to your recitation, of the Quran, yester-night, you would have felt delighted. You are in fact endowed with a sweet voice like that of David himself

Narrated Qatada: Anas was asked, How was the recitation, of the Quran, of the Prophet?' He replied, It was characterized by the prolongation of certain sounds. He then recited: In the Name of Allah, the Most Beneficent, the Most Merciful prolonging the pronunciation of 'In the Name of Allah, 'the most Beneficent,' and 'the Most Merciful

Narrated Aisha: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, Such a person as recites the Quran and masters it by heart, will be with the noble righteous scribes, in Heaven. And such a person exerts himself to learn the Quran by heart, and recites it with great difficulty, will have a double reward

A'isha reported Allah's Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, as saying,: One who is proficient in the Quran is associated with the noble, upright, recording angels; and he who falters in it, and finds it difficult for him, will have two rewards

Narrated Abu Huraira: I said, O Allah's Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him! I hear many narrations from you but I forget them. He said, Spread your covering sheet. I spread my sheet and he moved both his hands as if scooping something and emptied them in the sheet and said, Wrap it. I wrapped it round my body, and since then I have never forgotten

Abu Huraira, Allah be pleased with him, reported Allah's Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, as saying: When a man dies, his acts come to an end, but three, recurring charity, or knowledge, by which people, benefit, or a pious son, who prays for him, for the deceased,

Narrated Aisha: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, Do good deeds properly, sincerely and moderately, and receive good news because one's good deeds will not make him enter Paradise. They asked, Even you, O Allah's Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him? He said, Even I, unless and until Allah bestows His pardon and Mercy on me

Suhaib reported that Allah's Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Strange are the ways of a believer for there is good in every affair of his and this is not the case with anyone else except in the case of a believer for if he has an occasion to feel delight, he thanks, God, thus there is a good for him in it, and if he gets into trouble and shows resignation, and endures it patiently, there is a good for him in it
Narrated Anas: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, The real patience is at the first stroke of a calamity

Narrated Abu Said Al-Khudri and Abu Huraira: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, No fatigue, nor disease, nor sorrow, nor sadness, nor hurt, nor distress befalls a Muslim, even if it were the prick he receives from a thorn, but that Allah expiates some of his sins for that
Jarir reported from Allah's Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him,: He who is deprived of tenderly feelings is in fact deprived of good

Narrated Masruq: We were sitting with Abdullah bin Amr who was narrating to us, Hadith,: He said, Allah's Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, was neither a Fahish nor a Mutafahhish, and he used to say, 'The best among you are the best in character, having good manners,
Narrated Abu Huraira: I heard Allah's Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, saying. By Allah! I ask for forgiveness from Allah and turn to Him in repentance more than seventy times a day

Al-Agharr al-Muzani who was from amongst the Companions of Allah's Apostle, peace and blessings be upon him, reported that Ibn 'Umar stated to him that Allah's Messenger, may peace 'be upon him, said: O people, seek repentance from Allah. Verily, I seek repentance from Him a hundred times a day
Abu Huraira reported Allah's Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, as saying: Allah, the Exalted and Glorious, said: My mercy excels My wrath

Narrated Ibn Umar: We were with the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and fresh dates of a palm tree were brought to him. On that he said, Amongst the trees, there is a tree which resembles a Muslim. I wanted to say that it was the datepalm tree but as I was the youngest of all, of them, I kept quiet. And then the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, It is the date-palm tree

Narrated Usama bin Zaid: Allah's Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, used to put me on, one of, his thighs and put Al-Hasan bin Ali on his other thigh, and then embrace us and say, O Allah! Please be Merciful to them, as I am merciful to them

Narrated Aisha: A bedouin came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and said, You, people, kiss the boys! We don't kiss them. The Prophet said, I cannot put mercy in your heart after Allah has taken it away from it
Narrated Jarir bin Abdullah: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, He who is not merciful to others, will not be treated mercifully

Narrated Abu Huraira: I heard Allah's Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, saying, Allah divided Mercy into one hundred parts. He kept ninety nine parts with Him and sent down one part to the earth, and because of that, its one single part, His Creations are merciful to each other, so that even the mare lifts up its hoofs away from its baby animal, lest it should trample on it

Narrated Abdullah bin 'Abi Qatada: My father said, The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, 'When I stand for prayer, I intend to prolong it but on hearing the cries of a child, I cut it short, as I dislike to trouble the child's mother

Narrated Ibn Abbas: When the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, arrived at Mecca, some boys of the tribe of Bani Abdul Muttalib went to receive him, and the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, made one of them ride in front of him and the other behind him

Narrated Um Khalid bint Khalid: When I came from Ethiopia, to Medina, I was a young girl. Allah's Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, made me wear a sheet having marks on it. Allah's Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, was rubbing those marks with his hands saying, Sanah! Sanah! i.e. good, good,
And in truth We have made the Quran easy to remember; but is there any that remembereth?
Then exalted be Allah, the True King! And hasten not, O Muhammad, with the Quran ere its revelation hath been perfected unto thee, and say: My Lord! Increase me in knowledge.
Stir not thy tongue herewith to hasten it.
And, it is, a Quran that We have divided, that thou mayst recite it unto mankind at intervals, and We have revealed it by, successive, revelation.
And when the Quran is recited, give ear to it and pay heed, that ye may obtain mercy.
Read: In the name of thy Lord Who createth,
Who teacheth by the pen, Teacheth man that which he knew not.
The Beneficent Hath made known the Quran.
This is, a Scripture that We have revealed unto thee, full of blessing, that they may ponder its revelations, and that men of understanding may reflect.
Will they then not meditate on the Quran, or are there locks on the hearts?
O mankind! There hath come unto you an exhortation from your Lord, a balm for that which is in the breasts, a guidance and a mercy for believers.

Is he who payeth adoration in the watches of the night, prostrate and standing, bewaring of the Hereafter and hoping for the mercy of his Lord, to be accounted equal with a disbeliever? Say, unto them, O Muhammad,: Are those who know equal with those who know not? But only men of understanding will pay heed.

O ye who believe! when it is said unto you: Make room! in assemblies, then make room; Allah will make way for you, hereafter. And when it is said: Come up higher! go up higher; Allah will exalt those who believe among you, and those who have knowledge, to high ranks. Allah is informed of what ye do.
O ye who believe! Seek help in steadfastness and prayer. Lo! Allah is with the steadfast.

Say: O My bondmen who believe! Observe your duty to your Lord. For those who do good in this world there is good, and Allah's earth is spacious. Verily the steadfast will be paid their wages without stint.
But lo! with hardship goeth ease,
Endure thou patiently, O Muhammad. Thine endurance is only by, the help of, Allah. Grieve not for them, and be not in distress because of that which they devise.
Therefore remember Me, I will remember you. Give thanks to Me, and reject not Me.

And verily We gave Luqman wisdom, saying: Give thanks unto Allah; and whosoever giveth thanks, he giveth thanks for, the good of, his soul. And whosoever refuseth - Lo! Allah is Absolute, Owner of Praise.

Thy Lord hath decreed, that ye worship none save Him, and, that ye show, kindness to parents. If one of them or both of them attain old age with thee, say not Fie unto them nor repulse them, but speak unto them a gracious word.
And lower unto them the wing of submission through mercy, and say: My Lord! Have mercy on them both as they did care for me when I was little.
We sent thee not save as a mercy for the peoples.

It was by the mercy of Allah that thou wast lenient with them, O Muhammad, for if thou hadst been stern and fierce of heart they would have dispersed from round about thee. So pardon them and ask forgiveness for them and consult with them upon the conduct of affairs. And when thou art resolved, then put thy trust in Allah. Lo! Allah loveth those who put their trust, in Him.

And when those who believe in Our revelations come unto thee, say: Peace be unto you! Your Lord hath prescribed for Himself mercy, that whoso of you doeth evil through ignorance and repenteth afterward thereof and doeth right, for him, lo! He is Forgiving, Merciful.
And they are ordered naught else than to serve Allah, keeping religion pure for Him, as men by nature upright, and to establish worship and to pay the poor-due. That is true religion.
Say: Lo! my worship and my sacrifice and my living and my dying are for Allah, Lord of the Worlds.
O ye who believe! Guard your duty to Allah, and speak words straight to the point;
Seest thou not how Allah coineth a similitude: A goodly saying, as a goodly tree, its root set firm, its branches reaching into heaven,
The good deed and the evil deed are not alike. Repel the evil deed with one which is better, then lo! he, between whom and thee there was enmity, will become, as though he was a bosom friend.
Be guardians of your prayers, and of the midmost prayer, and stand up with devotion to Allah.
Successful indeed are the believers Who are humble in their prayers,
My Lord! Make me to establish proper worship, and some of my posterity, also,; our Lord! and accept my prayer.
Moses, said: My Lord! relieve my mind And ease my task for me; And loose a knot from my tongue, That they may understand my saying.
We verily created man and We know what his soul whispereth to him, and We are nearer to him than his jugular vein.
And whoso doeth good an atom's weight will see it then,
When ye are greeted with a greeting, greet ye with a better than it or return it. Lo! Allah taketh count of all things.
A kind word with forgiveness is better than almsgiving followed by injury. Allah is Absolute, Clement.
O ye who believe! Remember Allah with much remembrance.

He it is Who hath sent among the unlettered ones a messenger of their own, to recite unto them His revelations and to make them grow, and to teach them the Scripture and wisdom, though heretofore they were indeed in error manifest,
And lo! thou art of a tremendous nature.
Verily in the messenger of Allah ye have a good example for him who looketh unto Allah and the Last Day, and remembereth Allah much.

Bismillaah. Today we begin the riwayah of Warsh, from Imam Nafi of Madinah.
Imam Nafi was the great Quran teacher of Madinah. Warsh, Uthman ibn Saeed of Egypt, travelled to him and learnt his reading.
Today Warsh is recited across North and West Africa. It is the same Quran: the differences are in how some words are said, and in a few words.
In Hafs, the mim of the plural, as in alayhim and antum, has a sukoon.
Warsh joins this mim to a long u, but only when the next word begins with a hamzah.
Listen for the long oo at the end of the word, running into the hamzah.
When a word ends in a silent letter and the next word begins with a hamzah, Warsh drops the hamzah.
Its vowel moves back onto the silent letter: qad aflaha is read qada flaha, and al-ard is read alard.
The Warsh mushaf writes the hamzah’s alif bare, with no hamzah sign.
Listen to the letter before the hamzah: it carries the vowel, and there is no catch of a hamzah.
In many words Warsh changes a silent hamzah into a long vowel: yu'minoon is read yoominoon, and ya'tee is read yaatee.
The mushaf writes the vowel letter in place of the hamzah.
Listen for a smooth long vowel where Ḥafs has the stop of a hamzah.
When one word ends in a hamzah and the next begins with one, Warsh keeps the first and eases the second.
The eased hamzah is said lightly. The Warsh mushaf marks it with a dot instead of the hamzah sign.
Listen where the two words meet: only one hamzah is said clearly.
Warsh reads many alifs leaning towards ee: a sound between aa and ee.
This is in words ending in alif maqsoorah, like moosaa and ad-duhaa, and in some alifs before a final raa with kasrah.
The Warsh mushaf marks it with a dot under the letter.
Listen to the marked letter: its vowel leans, or is only partly said.
In many places Warsh reads the yaa of my and me with a fatha, where Hafs reads it silent: innee a'lamu is read inniya a'lamu.
In a few places it is the other way round. Each is learnt word by word.
Listen for the short ya at the end of the word.
In some words Warsh adds a yaa at the end that is not written in the rasm, when reading on: ad-daa'i is read ad-daa'ee.
The mushaf writes it as a small yaa.
Listen for the long ee at the end of the word when the reciter carries on.
In some words Warsh has different letters from Hafs: maaliki is read maliki, and some verbs change person.
These are learnt word by word. I can hear these when you recite, so read them carefully.
Listen for the different word, and read it as the mushaf writes it.
Some words keep their letters but change their vowels in Warsh.
These are learnt word by word, from the mushaf and from the reciter.

Bismillaah. Today we begin the riwayah of Qaloon, from Imam Nafi of Madinah.
Qaloon, Eesa ibn Meena, was a student of Imam Nafi in Madinah, and his stepson. Nafi gave him this name, which means good.
Today Qaloon is recited in Libya and Tunisia. It is close to Warsh, as both come from Nafi, but lighter in its hamzahs and its long vowels.
When a word ends in a long vowel and the next word begins with a hamzah, Hafs stretches the vowel four or five counts.
The official mushaf of Qaloon leaves out the madd sign there: the vowel keeps its natural length, two counts.
Qaloon is also transmitted with a moderate lengthening here. Ask your teacher which to use.
Listen to the long vowel before the hamzah: two counts, not stretched.
Some words begin with two hamzahs: a-andhartahum, a-anta, a-idhaa.
Qaloon eases the second hamzah, saying it lightly, between a hamzah and a vowel letter.
And Qaloon puts an alif between the two. The mushaf writes it as a small alif after the first hamzah.
Listen for the long aa after the first hamzah, then a soft second hamzah.
When one word ends in a hamzah and the next begins with one, Qaloon does not say both fully.
If both have a fatha, the first is dropped: jaa-a amruna is read jaa amruna. With two kasras or two dammas, the first is eased.
If the two vowels differ, the second is eased, or turned into a waaw or a yaa.
In some words Qaloon says the hamzah differently from Hafs.
It may be eased, left out, or said where Hafs has none. These are learnt word by word.
Listen to the hamzah in the highlighted word: softened, left out, or added.
In a few words the Qaloon mushaf puts a dot to show a vowel said only partly.
In seeya and seeyat, the kasrah of the seen is mixed with a trace of dammah. In yakhissimoon the vowel is said quickly.
In many places Qaloon reads the yaa of my and me with a fatha, where Hafs reads it silent: innee a'lamu is read inniya a'lamu.
In some words Qaloon adds a yaa at the end that is not written in the rasm, when reading on: ad-daa'i is read ad-daa'ee.
In some words Qaloon has different letters from Hafs: maaliki is read maliki, and some verbs change person.
Some words keep their letters but change their vowels in Qaloon.
Bismillaah. Today we begin the riwayah of ad-Doori, from Imam Abu Amr of Basra.
Abu Amr was the imam of the readers of Basra. His student al-Yazeedi taught his reading to ad-Doori.
Today ad-Doori is recited in Sudan and parts of West Africa. You will notice the leaning alif, and letters that merge.
Abu Amr merges some silent letters into the next letter: the daal of qad, the dhaal of idh, and the taa of she.
The merged letter is not said; the next letter is said doubled. The mushaf writes a shaddah on it.
Listen to where the two words meet: one letter, said doubled.
Abu Amr leans many alifs towards ee. In some words fully, in others only between aa and ee.
Most often in an alif before a final raa with kasrah, as in an-naar and al-kaafireen, and in words ending in alif maqsoorah.
The mushaf marks it with a dot under the letter.
ad-Doori eases the second hamzah, saying it lightly, between a hamzah and a vowel letter.
And ad-Doori puts an alif between the two. The mushaf writes it as a small alif after the first hamzah.
When one word ends in a hamzah and the next begins with one, ad-Doori does not say both fully.
If the two have the same vowel, Abu Amr drops the first: jaa-a amruna is read jaa amruna.
In some words ad-Doori says the hamzah differently from Hafs.
In many places ad-Doori reads the yaa of my and me with a fatha, where Hafs reads it silent: innee a'lamu is read inniya a'lamu.
In some words ad-Doori adds a yaa at the end that is not written in the rasm, when reading on: ad-daa'i is read ad-daa'ee.
In some words ad-Doori has different letters from Hafs: maaliki is read maliki, and some verbs change person.
Some words keep their letters but change their vowels in ad-Doori.
Bismillaah. Today we begin the riwayah of as-Soosi, from Imam Abu Amr of Basra.
As-Soosi learnt the reading of Abu Amr from al-Yazeedi, as ad-Doori did. The two share most rules.
As-Soosi is known for the great merging, where a letter at the end of a word merges into the same letter at the start of the next.
As-Soosi merges a letter at the end of a word into the same, or a close, letter at the start of the next, even when it has a vowel.
So ar-raheemi maaliki is read ar-raheem-maaliki. The mushaf writes a shaddah on the first letter of the second word.
Reciters also read these with a trace of the dropped vowel. Listen to your reciter, and ask your teacher.
The official mushaf of as-Soosi leaves out the madd sign there: the vowel keeps its natural length, two counts.
as-Soosi is also transmitted with a moderate lengthening here. Ask your teacher which to use.
In many words as-Soosi changes a silent hamzah into a long vowel: yu'minoon is read yoominoon, and ya'tee is read yaatee.
Abu Amr leans many alifs towards ee, especially before a final raa with kasrah: an-naar, al-kaafireen.
And in many words ending in alif maqsoorah. The mushaf marks it with a dot under the letter.
as-Soosi eases the second hamzah, saying it lightly, between a hamzah and a vowel letter.
And as-Soosi puts an alif between the two. The mushaf writes it as a small alif after the first hamzah.

In some words as-Soosi has different letters from Hafs: maaliki is read maliki, and some verbs change person.
Some words keep their letters but change their vowels in as-Soosi.
Bismillaah. Today we begin the riwayah of Shoubah, from Imam Aasim of Kufa.
Aasim is the same imam as Hafs. Shoubah, Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash, was his other famous student.
So Shoubah is the closest riwayah to Hafs. The differences are mostly in particular words, which we learn one by one.
Shoubah leans the alif towards ee in some particular words, such as ra-aa, he saw, and adraaka.
These are learnt word by word. The mushaf marks them with a dot under the letter.
In a few places Hafs makes a short pause, a sakt, as in man raaq and bal raan.
Shoubah reads on without the pause, so the letters merge: mar-raaq, bar-raan.
In some words Shoubah says the hamzah differently from Hafs.
In some words Shoubah has different letters from Hafs: maaliki is read maliki, and some verbs change person.
Some words keep their letters but change their vowels in Shoubah.
Bismillaah. Today we begin the riwayah of al-Bazzi, from Imam Ibn Katheer of Makkah.
Ibn Katheer was the imam of the readers of Makkah. Al-Bazzi was a reader and muezzin of the Haram, who carried his reading.
You will hear the long vowels joined to the pronouns, and some doubled letters. Let us take them one at a time.
al-Bazzi joins this mim to a long u before any letter with a vowel: alayhimoo, antumoo.
Before a silent letter, as in alayhimul qitaal, the mim takes a short vowel only, as in Hafs.
Listen for the long oo after the meem.
The pronoun ha, meaning him or it, after a silent letter: Hafs reads it short, as in feehi and minhu.
al-Bazzi reads it long: feehee, minhoo. The mushaf writes a small yaa or waaw after it.
Listen for the long vowel after the haa.
The official mushaf of al-Bazzi leaves out the madd sign there: the vowel keeps its natural length, two counts.
A long vowel inside one word, before a hamzah, is still stretched, as in jaa-a and as-samaa-i.
In thirty one places al-Bazzi doubles the taa at the start of a verb after a word that ends in a vowel: wa laa tayammamoo is read wa lat-tayammamoo.
The mushaf writes a shaddah on the taa.
